subject: Clarify SOC 2 Type II applicability across runtime variants (hosted / dedicated / VPC)
messages:
From: Lisa Gomez <lisa@finexa.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: ThirdParty Audit <audit@thirdpartyaudit.com>, security@finexa.com
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 scope question: runtime variants and evidence needed

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. We're starting our final control mapping for Finexa ahead of the procurement kickoff. A couple of quick questions on scope so we can tell procurement and the auditors what to expect: 

1) Does Redwood's current SOC 2 Type II (most recently issued for period 2027-01-01 to 2027-12-31) cover customer traffic served from Dedicated pools that are in a reserved capacity model, or is the Type II strictly scoped to the hosted/shared runtime only?

2) For customers who are moving from Hosted to Dedicated (or to a Private VPC), do you provide a bridge letter or other attestation that covers the transition period, and if so what evidence do you typically require from us?

3) Our auditor asked whether Private/VPC deployments can be included under Redwood's report if we enable the Redwood Private control plane (customer-managed networking) — or whether an independent attestation is required.

I've attached our SIG-lite questionnaire and a short list of endpoints the auditor will want visibility into. Can we schedule a short call next week to walk through the pathing and required artifacts?

Regards,
Lisa Gomez
Head of Security Ops, Finexa
security@finexa.com

Attachments: Finexa-SIG-answers.xlsx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Gomez <lisa@finexa.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 scope question: runtime variants and evidence needed

Lisa —

Thanks for the clear note and the SIG spreadsheet. Short answers up front: 

- Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report primarily covers our Hosted (multi-tenant) runtime and the control environment for the Redwood control plane for the report period stated.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) can be covered provided the customer instance is backed by a dedicated pool with documented tenant isolation and the pool was onboarded and operated during the report period. That typically requires us to include the dedicated pool in the auditor's sampling universe.
- Private/VPC/on-prem deployments generally require a separate attestation path; in many cases customers obtain a bridge letter from Redwood that explains which controls we continue to operate and which controls are customer-managed for the audited period. The bridge letter is not a replacement for a Type II report for an on-premises deployment but often suffices for specific control domains when combined with customer evidence.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please confirm the approximate cutover date for your migration to Dedicated/VPC and whether you used Dedicated resources during the 2027 audit window.
2) We'll assemble a proposed evidence checklist and a draft bridge letter for review (will include control ownership mapping).
3) If helpful, Marissa (cc'd) can share a high-level topology and evidence expectations for dedicated pools.

I can do 30 minutes next Wed or Thu afternoon PT. What works for you?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Lisa / Kimberly —

Adding some technical detail so your auditor can map controls to runtime artifacts. Key points: 

- Dedicated pools: these are physical/virtualized GPU clusters reserved to a single customer tenancy. For audit inclusion we need:
  * Start/end dates showing the pool was active during the reporting window
  * Tenant isolation proof (routing table excerpts, group membership, pool assignment records)
  * Patch and configuration baselines for the pool nodes

- Hosted (shared): fully covered in the Type II report; sampling includes multi-tenant requests and our standard change management artifacts.

- Private / VPC: what varies is the control ownership split. Example mapping:
  * Network perimeter & customer-managed network connectors — owned by customer (we document integration patterns)
  * Key management — if customer supplies KMS/HSM we map the responsibility in the bridge letter

I'm attaching a simplified topology (hosting-topology-v2.png) and an evidence checklist (hosting-evidence-checklist-2028.xlsx) that auditors have accepted in the past. If you can share the migration cutover timestamp and a list of endpoints you'll be using for processing, I will pre-fill the checklist and mark which items Redwood can produce vs which we'd expect from you.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
